_meta.description: Judgment Metric Registry — Phase 0 deliverable 0.9. Documents all analyst-judgment-bound metrics with assigned handling mechanisms. Zero unresolved gating/gate-triggering metrics required for Phase 0 exit.

1.label: Fully Computable
1.description: Computable from data without analyst judgment. Denominator stable. No allocation required.

2.label: Computable with Documented Judgment
2.description: Computable but specific parameters or allocation choices require analyst judgment. Judgment documented in AIMS Mode A.

3.label: Escalation Flag
3.description: Too uncertain for automated gating. Triggers human review when materiality threshold exceeded. Human decision is authoritative. CANNOT gate phase transitions or trigger Confirmation Gate automatically.
3.confirmation_gate_triggering: FORBIDDEN (may trigger human review request only)

metrics.notes: Fully computable. Denominator stable. Content_category classification is a known limitation but not an analyst judgment call.

documented_judgments.judgment: For multi-vector incidents, primary attack_vector is assigned using detection_method as tiebreaker. If detection_method is inconclusive, classify as the vector with the highest financial_impact_usd precedent in the same period.
documented_judgments.rationale: Prevents arbitrary allocation; ties the decision to observable data

metrics.notes: Mechanism 2 because multi-vector incident allocation requires judgment. Documented above.

confirmation_gate_use: no — count metric, not direct financial exposure

documented_judgments.judgment: Behavioral deviation threshold: 2σ on ≥2 dimensions simultaneously, within 7-day window of fraud_incident. Parameters validated quarterly by Statistician Agent.
documented_judgments.rationale: Threshold balances precision vs. recall. Lower threshold increases false positives during product changes.

confirmation_gate_use: yes — trend escalation (SPRT positive) triggers gate
metrics.notes: Count metric, fully computable. SPRT configuration parameters (null/alternative hypothesis rates) are validated by Statistician Agent quarterly — not real-time judgment.

gating_use: FORBIDDEN — mechanism 3 cannot gate phase transitions
confirmation_gate_use: FORBIDDEN — may trigger review request only when exposure > $500k
metrics.resolution_rationale: Indirect and legal liability components are model estimates with 40-80% confidence intervals. Automating decisions on estimates of this uncertainty would be unsafe. Human review at $500k threshold is the correct governance.

documented_judgments.judgment: CI bounds set at [-40%, +80%] around point estimate, reflecting asymmetric uncertainty in downstream harm costs. Regulatory penalty component (actual enforced fines) is separated as a higher-confidence sub-component.
documented_judgments.rationale: Actual fines are confirmed; indirect/legal components are estimates. Separating them by confidence level makes the uncertainty transparent.

metrics.notes: This is the only Mechanism 3 metric. It cannot gate phase transitions or trigger the Confirmation Gate automatically. This satisfies Phase 0 exit criterion (e).

gating_use: no — derived metric, used for investment prioritization, not gating

documented_judgments.judgment: Cost allocation assumes uniform cost per incident within attack_vector × period. This understates cost for high-severity incidents and overstates it for low-severity ones. When used for investment decisions, always report with distribution (p50, p95) not just mean.
documented_judgments.rationale: The uniform allocation is known to be wrong but is the only tractable allocation method without per-incident cost tracking.

phase_0_exit_criterion_check.criterion: (e) Judgment metric registry complete — zero unresolved gating/gate-triggering metrics
phase_0_exit_criterion_check.note: downstream_harm_exposure is Mechanism 3 but explicitly excluded from gating and gate-triggering. All other metrics are Mechanism 1 or 2 with documented judgments.
